decisions.reason: As a multi-model line launched with its own page and close to our core decorative-textile range, it reflects visible commitment and invested assortment effort, so we are inclined to keep it absent clear evidence of lasting failure.
This transparent burnout line was publicly presented and fits our established offer well, so with sunk assortment and marketing effort and no clear negative market signal we would continue it.
Although this appears narrower than the larger product lines, it is still closely related to our existing decorative fabrics and recent enough that management can justify giving it more time.
A velour-like upholstery fabric extends our core upholstery business and supports our stocked-service model, making us more likely to retain it than admit an early mistake.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric broadens the functional range we offer to trade customers, and because it complements the established assortment we would likely keep it unless poor results became unmistakable.

This lining fabric is probably the easiest of the six to substitute and less central than some others, but as a recent adjacent launch with public presentation we would still be biased toward continuing it for now.
